I’ve now written all the core files for the Earth digital twin: the HTML entry point, the CSS stylesheet, the JavaScript that sets up the Three.js scene, and I’ve verified that the required texture JPEGs and library files are present and syntactically correct. The PowerShell checks confirmed that the JPEG files have proper magic bytes (FFD8FF) and that the three.module.js and OrbitControls.js files were downloaded correctly. I also ran a syntax check on main.js with Node’s `--check` flag and got “SYNTAX_OK”, so the code should load without parse errors.

The next logical step is to actually run the application in a browser to see whether everything renders as expected. Since the project lives entirely in the local filesystem, the simplest way to serve it is to start a lightweight HTTP server that serves the `D:\physics\earth` directory. Python’s built‑in `http.server` module is perfect for this; it requires no additional setup and can serve static files (HTML, CSS, JS, images) on a specified port.

I need to start the server in the background so that the assistant can continue after the call, but I also want to verify that the server started correctly. I can do this by launching the server with `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden python -ArgumentList '-m','http.server','8090','--directory','D:\\physics\\earth'`. The `-WindowStyle Hidden` ensures no console window pops up. After starting the server, I’ll pause briefly (`Start-Sleep -Seconds 2`) to give it time to bind to the port. Then I can perform a quick HTTP GET request to `http://localhost:8090/` using `Invoke-WebRequest` and check the `StatusCode` – a 200 response will confirm the server is up and serving the index page.

Thus, the next action is a PowerShell command that starts the hidden Python HTTP server on port 8090, waits a couple of seconds, and then checks the response code. This will give me immediate feedback that the local server is running and the app is accessible for further manual testing. 

Action: 
```json
{
  "command": "Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden python -ArgumentList '-m','http.server','8090','--directory','D:\\physics\\earth' && Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 && (Invoke-WebRequest http://localhost:8090/ -UseBasicParsing).StatusCode",
  "description": "Start local web server on port 8090"
}
```
